summary: Remote-controlled agent: hardcoded WebSocket gateway drives PTY/shell and SSH tunnels on the host
details: When the `whalent` bin is started, the daemon opens a persistent WebSocket to a hardcoded gateway at wss://memory.whalent.com/gw/sdk/ws and treats messages from that channel as commands. The bundle wires the gateway to PTY/shell primitives (@xterm/headless, node-pty, child_process) and to SSH-tunnel/proxy operations (`ssh.tunnel.open`, `proxy.open`), including forwards to local RDP (127.0.0.1:3389) and VNC (127.0.0.1:5900). The README documents that the gateway can issue upgrade and restart commands. Any party controlling memory.whalent.com or its gateway (the vendor, anyone who compromises it, or anyone who takes over the domain) can execute arbitrary commands on the host running the agent and pivot into local services via the tunnel primitives. The shipped runtime code (dist/index.cjs and the 4.8 MB dist/core.cjs) is produced with javascript-obfuscator (string-array rotation, hex identifier renaming, control-flow flattening), which hinders review of exactly what the gateway can command.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
